Hi all —

Thanks for sending this over, Olivia. I reviewed the redline and left line-by-line notes in the PDF. Summary of our position and proposed compromise language below (for ease of review we’ll also drop a tracked-changes DPA if you prefer):

1) Training/use of Customer Data
- BluePeak asks for an absolute prohibition on using any Customer Data for model training or improvement unless we have written consent.
- Redwood position: for Hosted customers we aim to retain limited telemetry/metric data to improve platform reliability; however, we routinely accept a contractual carve-out that prevents using Customer Data (as defined below) for training or model improvement.
- Proposed clause (single-sentence replacement for BluePeak’s Section 4.3):
  "Supplier shall not use Customer Data, as defined below, to train, fine-tune, or improve machine learning models or any derivative models, or for any model development purposes, except where Customer provides prior written consent. ‘Customer Data’ shall mean: (a) data expressly uploaded or submitted by Customer in the course of using the Service; and (b) any output generated by the Service that contains Customer-specific information; excluding aggregated and de-identified metrics that cannot be reasonably re-identified to Customer or individuals."
- Note: we are comfortable with that formulation for enterprise customers on any plan if they require the commitment; once accepted we will operationalize a ‘no-training’ flag for the account and enforce it across our pipelines.

2) Subprocessors and data transfers
- BluePeak requests 30 days’ notice and an ability to object to new subprocessors that will process EU personal data. Our standard: 15 days’ notice plus the right for Customer to object if they have a legitimate data-protection reason; if objection is raised, Supplier will use reasonable efforts to mitigate and, if not possible, parties will discuss alternatives (e.g., contractual safeguards, restricting processing to Dedicated instances).
- Proposed compromise language:
  "Supplier will provide Customer with prior written notice of any new Subprocessor that will have access to Customer Personal Data at least fifteen (15) days before such Subprocessor commences processing. Customer may object to a proposed Subprocessor within fifteen (15) days of receipt of such notice by providing reasonable details of the objection. If Customer objects on legitimate data protection grounds, Supplier will use commercially reasonable efforts to address Customer’s concerns, including offering additional contractual safeguards or technical controls, or transitioning the impacted processing to a Dedicated/Private environment where feasible."

3) Execution and next steps
- If BluePeak agrees to the above language we can accept their redline with these counterpoints and proceed to execution. We will prepare a clean DPA and provide a DocuSign envelope (or AdobeSign if you prefer).

Please let us know which is preferred, DocuSign or AdobeSign. If accepted, I’ll send a final tracked DPA for sign-off by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
